label: MEASURE_EVENTDATE_DURATIONINSECONDS
definition: A Measure Test, applied to a SingleRecord, that evaluates: What is the duration of dwc:eventDate in seconds? It returns: INTERNAL_PREREQUISITES_NOT_MET if dwc:eventDate is bdqval:Empty or if the value of dwc:eventDate is not a valid ISO 8601 date; otherwise RUN_HAS_RESULT with the result being the duration (sensu ISO 8601) expressed in the dwc:eventDate, in seconds.
description: What is the duration of dwc:eventDate in seconds?
notes: The duration of a day is 86400 seconds. Implementations should treat all days as 86400 seconds, but should include leap days (but not leap seconds) in durations that encompass them. Consumers should treat assertions about event date duration as approximations, see: https://xkcd.com/2867/
expectedResponse: INTERNAL_PREREQUISITES_NOT_MET if dwc:eventDate is bdqval:Empty or if the value of dwc:eventDate is not a valid ISO 8601 date; otherwise RUN_HAS_RESULT with the result being the duration (sensu ISO 8601) expressed in the dwc:eventDate, in seconds.
examples: [dwc:eventDate="1880-05-08/10": Response.status=RUN_HAS_RESULT, Response.result="259200", Response.comment="dwc:eventDate duration is 3 days = 259,200 seconds"],[dwc:eventDate="95": Response.status=INTERNAL_PREREQUISITES_NOT_MET, Response.comment="dwc:eventDate does not contain a valid ISO 8601-1:2019 date"]
references:

  • Wikipedia (2020) ISO 8601. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_8601
